title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ... ]
teaching_text:
Once again he speaks about the production of the word t[hat comes] from the mouth and is heard by the [ears]. He says [ ... ⟨p.261⟩ ... ] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.

Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.

This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.
gardner_synopsis: The process of forming a word is compared to the production of a coin.
editorial_notes: Removed Coptic manuscript line numbers embedded in the English text (e.g. the standalone “5”, “10”). Removed page/running-header artifacts (“267”, divider line, and “CHAPTER ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHT”). Converted the inline manuscript page marker “(261)” to ⟨p.261⟩ and preserved surrounding lacuna brackets as given. Left uncertain reading “sieve (?)” unchanged.
